summary.text: CA9 is the candidate on which omics, literature, external knowledge, single-cell and translational data agree most. It is strongly up in tumour RNA [gene=CA9; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=6.312], replicates in TCGA-KIRC, survives extrapolation to a pure tumour, and its tumour transcripts come from the cancer cells themselves rather than from stroma [gene=CA9; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.976]. Girentuximab-based antibody and imaging agents are already in clinical development, and the literature reports CA9 PET as a proof of concept for non-invasive detection. It is best read as a surface antigen and imaging biomarker rather than a dependency: DepMap shows no ccRCC dependency, and stomach enrichment in the normal-tissue proteome is a safety flag for any conjugate [gene=CA9; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; vital_organ_protein_ts_max=5.19].

A second tier of tumour-up, tractable candidates follows CA9, and in the target profile SCARB1, CD70, SLC16A3, NNMT and ENPP3 keep their places under random re-weighting. CD70 and ENPP3 already have clinical antibody or conjugate programmes; CD70 scores best for conjugate suitability among the controls but much of its signal also comes from infiltrating lymphocytes. NNMT has the cleanest case among the newer genes: its protein gain replicates in the independent confirmatory CPTAC cohort, both single-cell datasets place it in tumour cells, and high expression is linked to worse survival in TCGA. SLC16A3 (MCT4) and SCARB1 also replicate at the protein level, but their cell of origin differs between the two single-cell datasets, so their ranks overstate how well the source is known. None of these five has a selective DepMap dependency; the only selective dependency in the ranked set is the established target EPAS1 (HIF-2 alpha, belzutifan).

The strongest biomarker calls are different genes from the strongest targets. PSAT1, PCK1 and SLC6A19 are the most robust members of the biomarker profile, and they, ALDOB and SLC22A8 are all lower in tumour than in normal kidney: they mark lost proximal-tubule identity and are not drug targets. PSAT1 protein loss replicates in the confirmatory cohort, yet within tumours higher PSAT1 goes with worse survival, BAP1 mutation and the aggressive ccB state, so it reads as a subtype marker. ALDOB and SLC22A8 are literature-supported prognostic loss markers whose protective survival direction is borne out in TCGA. COXFA4L2 (NDUFA4L2) is a HIF-driven tumour-up marker with dense preclinical literature, but its mitochondrial location makes it a tissue biomarker rather than an antibody target.

The convergence ranking rewards literature and existing drugs, so it cannot put a little-studied gene on top. The discovery screen is where those genes appear, and two tumour-cell genes from it are identified and prioritised for experimental validation. COL23A1, a transmembrane collagen, is made mainly by RCC cells [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.881] and keeps a large increase when extrapolated to a pure tumour [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; rna_lfc_at_purity1=4.88]. It also replicates in TCGA-KIRC, has no clinical drug and shows no vital-organ protein enrichment. What is missing: surface display has not been confirmed experimentally, the AlphaFold model is low confidence, and there is no prognostic signal, no selective dependency, no confirmatory-cohort protein and no measure of heterogeneity across tumour cells; immunohistochemistry on tumour and normal tissue arrays plus surface proteomics would test it. RAB42, a small GTPase, is also made mostly by RCC cells [gene=RAB42; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.627] and persists in a pure tumour, but it is unlikely to be antibody-accessible, so knockdown or CRISPR experiments in ccRCC models are the natural next test. The best stroma candidates (OLFML2A, JAG2) are purity-robust but come from fibroblasts and endothelium, and the immune-track genes (MILR1, LILRB4, GAL3ST4) fade in a pure tumour, so their bulk signal is infiltration. Novel here means at most fifteen ccRCC papers and no clinical drug, not that nothing was published: the literature corpus held no relations for these genes, so earlier preclinical work cannot be excluded, and nothing here shows that targeting them would help a patient.

Across all layers the top-ranked new candidates are antigen, imaging or biomarker leads rather than vulnerabilities. The one selective cell-line dependency belongs to the established target EPAS1, the established VEGFR target KDR is endothelial rather than tumour-intrinsic, and in the trial data no gene separates the main treatment arms after correction.

omics.text: CPTAC tumour-versus-normal data separate two groups of genes. HIF-driven genes rise in tumour: CD70 is up at RNA and protein in CPTAC and strongly up in TCGA-KIRC [gene=CD70; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=7.09], and it shows no vital-organ protein enrichment [gene=CD70; type=normal_proteome; source=DATASET:GTEX-PROTEOME; vital_protein_ts_max=0.34]. The same tumour-up pattern holds for CA9, NNMT, ENPP3, SLC16A3 and SCARB1.

NNMT combines a strong tumour gain [gene=NNMT; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=4.685] with an adverse survival association in TCGA [gene=NNMT; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=0.301], so it is both a target lead and a prognostic biomarker.

Proximal-tubule genes fall in tumour: PSAT1, PCK1, SLC6A19 and ALDH6A1 are lost at RNA in TCGA-KIRC with concordant protein loss in CPTAC. These are biomarkers of lost tubule identity, not targets. Their survival associations point in different directions: high ALDH6A1 is favourable, whereas high PSAT1 within tumours is adverse, so each must be interpreted separately.

literature.text: Literature and data agree for CA9, CD70 and NNMT: all three are reported as tumour-enriched with therapeutic or imaging potential, and the data show tumour-up, purity-robust expression. The evidence for all three is preclinical or early translational: CA9 PET is a proof of concept awaiting prospective validation, CD70 radiotracers are preclinical, and the NNMT inhibitors described are chemistry papers without ccRCC efficacy data. The tubule-loss markers ALDOB, SLC22A8 and UMOD are supported as diagnostic or prognostic markers, mostly by bioinformatic studies with limited immunohistochemistry.

The literature contradicts itself or the data for several genes. MT1G is lower in tumour, yet high expression is reported as adverse. ABAT is a reported tumour suppressor that one study says predicts poor prognosis. PFKP is up in tumour, yet low expression is linked to poor survival. FCER1G is described as abundant in tumour, but the data show the signal is immune-cell derived. Several highly ranked data candidates (SCARB1, PIGR, ENPP3 and a series of tubular transporters) have no literature relations in this corpus, and even EPAS1 and VHL appear only at sentence level, so the literature stream under-represents known biology.

external.text: Open Targets, UniProt and DepMap divide the leading candidates into antigen and dependency cases. CA9, CD70 and ENPP3 are membrane antigens with clinical antibody or conjugate programmes (girentuximab, cusatuzumab and vorsetuzumab mafodotin, AGS-16C3F) and no ccRCC dependency, so their case rests on antibody, conjugate or imaging approaches. EPAS1 is the only ranked gene with a ccRCC-selective DepMap dependency, although its q-value is borderline, and belzutifan is approved against it. VHL is the top Open Targets association and the recurrent driver, mutated in about half of tumours; it explains the HIF programme but is not itself druggable.

SCARB1, NNMT and SLC16A3 are predicted tractable but have no clinical drug and no ccRCC dependency, so they are druggable-in-principle leads whose functional relevance is untested. For the down-regulated markers (ALDOB, SLC22A8, PIGR) the drugs annotated are transporter-directed and not antitumour, so tractability flags for them are not a reason to inhibit them.

cells.text: In single-cell RNA-seq, CA9 is tumour-cell intrinsic: RCC cells hold nearly all of its tumour transcripts [gene=CA9; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.976], and the paired tumour-versus-proximal-tubule comparison shows a large gain [gene=CA9; type=sc_tumor_vs_pt; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; log2fc=7.739].

NNMT has the most stable cell attribution of the genes checked: tumour cells dominate in both single-cell datasets [gene=NNMT; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_cell_share=0.97]. By contrast, SCARB1 is attributed to myeloid cells in one dataset and tumour cells in the other, and SLC16A3 to T and NK cells in one and tumour cells in the other, so their bulk tumour gain does not yet pin down the expressing cell.

Several bulk candidates are not tumour-intrinsic. KDR is almost entirely endothelial [gene=KDR; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.951], CD74 is a macrophage and antigen-presenting-cell gene, and CXCR4 is carried by T cells, so all three are microenvironment targets. EPAS1 transcripts sit largely in endothelium in the single-cell data [gene=EPAS1; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.365], which probably reflects poor capture of this transcript in RCC cells rather than its biology. CD70 is highest in RCC cells but also present in T cells and Tregs, so it is tumour-enriched rather than tumour-exclusive.

spatial.text: In Visium sections, spots with high CA9 are surrounded by RCC-rich neighbours [gene=CA9; type=spatial_neighborhood; source=DATASET:LI2022-VISIUM; cell_group=RCC; log2_enrichment=0.381] with a smaller macrophage enrichment, and the composition-corrected in situ expresser is the RCC cell, consistent with the single-cell attribution.
KDR is endothelial in situ as well, with essentially no contribution from RCC cells, which confirms that anti-VEGFR therapy acts on the tumour vasculature rather than on the cancer cells.

structure.text: The AlphaFold CA9 monomer is of moderate confidence [gene=CA9; type=alphafold_model; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; mean_plddt=76.56], its top detected cavity is small [gene=CA9; type=structural_context; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; volume_a3=126.8], and the detected cavities recover part of the experimentally observed ligand-contact residues [gene=CA9; type=ligand_site_validation; source=PDBe-KB ligand sites (experimental holo structures); recall=0.5]. These are descriptive structural heuristics on a predicted monomer: they do not identify a degron, a ligase interface or a degrader, and no curated experimental degron or ternary-complex reference was used for any candidate.

The COL23A1 model is low confidence [gene=COL23A1; type=alphafold_model; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; mean_plddt=58.91] and shows only a shallow cavity, so it offers no small-molecule structural handle; an antibody against its extracellular domain is the plausible modality, although this heuristic does not exclude others.

discovery.text: COL23A1 leads the tumour-cell track. It encodes a transmembrane collagen, and in the single-cell data most of its tumour transcripts come from RCC cells [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.881]. The gain survives extrapolation to a pure tumour [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; rna_lfc_at_purity1=4.88], so it is not an infiltration artefact. It replicates in TCGA-KIRC, the normal-tissue proteome shows no vital-organ enrichment, and it has few ccRCC papers and no clinical drug. It is not prognostic in TCGA, DepMap shows no selective dependency, there is no confirmatory-cohort protein measurement, and its surface display and heterogeneity across tumour cells have not been measured. It is a data-ranked hypothesis for an antibody-based approach, to be tested first by immunohistochemistry on tumour and normal tissue arrays.

RAB42, a small GTPase involved in vesicle traffic, is the second tumour-track candidate. Most of its tumour transcripts come from RCC cells [gene=RAB42; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.627]. It is up in TCGA-KIRC and robust to purity, with no survival signal and no clinical drug. Its surface status is unknown and it is most likely intracellular, so an antibody route is unlikely, and there is no dependency evidence; knockdown or CRISPR experiments in ccRCC models are the natural first test.

The stroma track is led by OLFML2A, a secreted protein made mainly by fibroblasts [gene=OLFML2A; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=stroma; source_share=0.647], and JAG2, a Notch ligand whose signal is only partly endothelial [gene=JAG2; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=stroma; source_share=0.487]. Both replicate in TCGA and are purity-robust, but OLFML2A has colon expression and JAG2 already has some ccRCC literature and heart expression. The immune track (MILR1, LILRB4, GAL3ST4) consists of macrophage genes whose fold change shrinks to near nothing in a pure tumour [gene=MILR1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=immune; rna_lfc_at_purity1=0.414], so their bulk gain reflects infiltration; GAL3ST4 is in addition a Golgi protein out of antibody reach. None of the discovery candidates is a selective dependency, and all remain data-ranked hypotheses.

validation.text: The independent layers strengthen CA9, CD70, NNMT, ENPP3, SCARB1 and SLC16A3: all replicate their tumour gain in TCGA-KIRC and survive extrapolation to a pure tumour. In the independent label-free confirmatory CPTAC cohort, the protein calls replicate for NNMT [gene=NNMT; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=4.776], SLC16A3 [gene=SLC16A3; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=3.551], SCARB1 [gene=SCARB1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=2.334] and, as a loss, PSAT1 [gene=PSAT1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-3.946]. Only these four were checked in the confirmatory cohort in this run; the known non-replicating candidate HK2 was not re-examined, and the one PSAT1 phosphosite measurable in both cohorts did not replicate.

Prognosis, genetics and dependency weaken most of the leading targets as functional vulnerabilities. CA9, CD70 and SCARB1 carry no survival signal in TCGA, whereas NNMT and PSAT1 are adverse and ALDOB and ALDH6A1 favourable. VHL is the recurrent somatic driver and none of the leading targets is recurrently mutated. In DepMap only EPAS1 shows a ccRCC-selective dependency, so the antigen candidates rest on expression restriction rather than need. Protein-adjusted kinase activity was not assessed for these candidates in this run, and none of them is a kinase. The purity check removes the immune-track discovery genes, whose bulk gain disappears in a pure tumour.

robustness.text: Random re-weighting of the evidence streams separates stable from weight-dependent calls. In the target profile, SCARB1, CA9, SLC16A3, CD70, NNMT, ENPP3 and FABP6 stay in the top ten in most draws with narrow rank intervals, so their position does not hinge on the chosen weights. CYP2J2, HK2 and ANGPTL4 sit at the edge of the top ten, and HK2, SLC16A3 and SLC2A1 would leave the top twenty-five without the tumour-up omics stream. In the biomarker profile, PSAT1, PCK1 and SLC6A19 are robust, whereas SLPI, DUSP9, VWF and L1CAM have wide intervals and depend on single streams such as prognosis.

In the overall convergence score only CA9 and COXFA4L2 are robust top-ten members. ALDOB, CD70, SLC22A8, SCARB1, PIGR, NNMT, UMOD and FABP1 move considerably, and several of them, including NNMT and UMOD, drop out of the top twenty-five if the literature stream is removed. Because the overall score mixes target and biomarker evidence, target calls in this report follow the target profile and biomarker calls follow the biomarker profile.

treatment.text: In IMmotion150, higher CA9 is associated with longer benefit on sunitinib [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.sunitinib.log_hr_per_sd=-0.336], but not significantly, and it does not separate the combination from sunitinib [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_between_arms.padj=0.917]. It is a lead from a small arm, not a predictor.

No gene examined separates the two main IMmotion150 arms after correction. Higher PCK1 is associated with earlier progression on atezolizumab plus bevacizumab [gene=PCK1; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.atezolizumab_bevacizumab.log_hr_per_sd=0.22], but the association is not significant after correction and flips direction in other arms. For NNMT and EPAS1 only the nivolumab trials had data, and neither separates nivolumab from everolimus after correction. These are associations, not treatment-selection markers.

subtypes.text: CA9 is a subgroup candidate for PBRM1-mutant tumours, higher in mutants across CPTAC RNA, CPTAC protein and TCGA RNA [gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; PBRM1.cptac_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=0.971], although the protein effect is modest. PSAT1 is higher in BAP1-mutant tumours [gene=PSAT1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; BAP1.tcga_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=1.711] and tracks the ccB state, and PCK1 is lower in ccB than in ccA [gene=PCK1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; ccA_ccB.tcga_rna.ccB_minus_ccA_log2=-2.581] at RNA but not significantly at protein. Subtype differences in bulk tissue can partly reflect differing immune and stromal content, so they need confirmation in purified tumour cells.

adc.text: Among the known-target controls, CD70 scores best for conjugate suitability [gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.746], but it lacks Human Protein Atlas staining data, so its normal-tissue safety rests on the proteome alone. ENPP3 is surface-confirmed but normal kidney stains at the top level [gene=ENPP3; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; kidney_staining_level=3.0], with duodenum staining too. CA9 has surface topology but a gastric on-target risk. SCARB1 is surface-confirmed, but adrenal staining is high and few tumour cells express it in the weakest donors [gene=SCARB1; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=7.1], so a conjugate would face a narrow window. A suitability score does not show that a conjugate would work.

immune.text: Deconvolution assigns much of the CD70 signal to immune cells [gene=CD70; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.654], and CD70 rises with CD8 T cells and Tregs, so it marks hot, infiltrated tumours as well as tumour cells; a CD70 conjugate would also hit infiltrating lymphocytes. Its association with longer benefit on atezolizumab plus bevacizumab [gene=CD70; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; log_hr_atezolizumab_bevacizumab=-0.383] is reported without an adjusted p-value and is an association only. SLC16A3 also shows a large immune share [gene=SLC16A3; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.667] but no relation to CD8 T cells. CD74, CXCR4 and the immune-track discovery genes are immune-cell genes whose bulk gain tracks infiltration rather than tumour cells.

integration.text: Omics, literature and external knowledge converge on a HIF-driven, tumour-cell surface programme (CA9, CD70, ENPP3), with NNMT as the best-supported newer gene, and on a separate set of tubule-loss biomarkers (PSAT1, PCK1, ALDOB, SLC22A8). They diverge in three ways: literature-free data candidates such as SCARB1 rank high on omics and genetics alone; the literature reports prognostic directions that the data contradict for MT1G, ABAT and PFKP; and several bulk signals (CD70 partly, KDR, CD74, CXCR4, the immune discovery genes) come from the microenvironment rather than the tumour cell. In practice the candidates divide into antigen or imaging targets, biomarkers, and mechanism genes (VHL, EPAS1).

targets.rationale: Strongest convergence across all layers: tumour-cell intrinsic, purity-robust, replicated in TCGA, robust in the target profile, with clinical antibody and imaging agents. No dependency and a gastric on-target risk, so it is an antigen and imaging candidate.

Tumour-up, purity-robust surface antigen with clinical antibody and conjugate programmes and the best conjugate suitability among controls; ranked below CA9 because much of its signal also comes from infiltrating lymphocytes and it lacks normal-tissue staining data.

The best-supported newer gene: tumour-cell origin replicated in two single-cell datasets, protein gain replicated in the confirmatory cohort, adverse survival in TCGA and predicted small-molecule tractability. No ccRCC dependency, so its biomarker case is currently stronger than its target case.

Placed above its numeric rank because it is the only candidate with a ccRCC-selective DepMap dependency and has an approved drug (belzutifan); it ranks low because bulk and single-cell expression do not capture HIF-2 alpha protein stabilisation.
Tumour-up surface ectoenzyme with a clinical antibody-drug conjugate (AGS-16C3F) and robust target-profile rank; strong normal kidney and duodenum staining is the main limitation for a conjugate.

MCT4 lactate exporter, robust in the target profile and replicated at protein in the confirmatory cohort; ranked lower because its cell of origin is discordant between single-cell datasets, much of its signal is immune-assigned and there is no dependency.

Ranked below its first place in the target profile: tumour-up and replicated at protein, but cell attribution is discordant, few tumour cells express it in the weakest donors, adrenal staining is high and there is no dependency or literature support in this corpus.
Most robust member of the biomarker profile; protein loss replicates in the confirmatory cohort, while within tumours higher PSAT1 marks worse survival, BAP1 mutation and the ccB state.
Robust tubule-identity loss marker with concordant protein loss and lower RNA in ccB tumours; not a treatment-selection marker.
Strongly lost in tumour with a protective survival association that agrees with independent literature; a prognostic biomarker, not a target.

NDUFA4L2: robust top-ten convergence and dense preclinical HIF-mechanism literature; its mitochondrial location makes it a tissue biomarker rather than an antibody target, and its prognostic value rests on the literature.
Proximal-tubule transporter lost in tumour, with loss linked to worse survival in both literature and TCGA; annotated drugs are transporter-directed and not antitumour.

Exploratory: tumour-cell-derived, purity-robust transmembrane collagen replicated in TCGA with no clinical drug; the main limitation is that surface display, normal-tissue staining, heterogeneity and any functional dependency are unmeasured.
Exploratory: tumour-cell-derived, purity-robust and replicated in TCGA; the main limitation is that it is probably intracellular, so not antibody-accessible, and has no dependency evidence.

limitations.text: Passing the automatic checks establishes evidence linkage and numeric bindings, not complete scientific validation; causal and therapeutic interpretations remain hypotheses.
No leading target except the established EPAS1 shows a selective DepMap dependency, and cell lines grown in two dimensions under-represent HIF-2 biology.
Single-cell attribution rests on two datasets with few paired donors; SCARB1 and SLC16A3 disagree between them, and the CD70 single-cell rows had no evidence ids.
Treatment-response associations come from small trial arms; none separates the main arms after correction, and NNMT and EPAS1 lacked IMmotion150 data.

The literature corpus is a few hundred mostly retrospective abstracts and has no relations for several highly ranked genes, including EPAS1, VHL, SCARB1 and the discovery candidates; earlier preclinical work on those genes cannot be excluded.

Only four candidates were checked in the confirmatory proteome cohort, kinase activity and phosphosites were not examined per candidate, and MET, EGFR, FABP6 and CYP2J2 were not profiled by the cell or translational agents.
Structural-context scores are monomer heuristics on predicted models and do not identify degrons, ligase compatibility or degraders.
